notes: Official sites could not be read: textbooksonline.tn.nic.in (robots disallowed for the fetch tool), tnschools.gov.in/scert (JavaScript-rendered), the official cloudfront e-book HTML/PDF links (fetch errors), textbookcorp.tn.gov.in price list (robots disallowed), dge.tn.gov.in (no syllabus/blueprint notices visible). The chapter and section list comes from a copy of the official TNTBESC/SCERT PDF (Revised Edition 2021 front matter) hosted on cdn1.byjus.com. Chapters are marked verified:true on that basis.
Single volume confirmed from the front matter: no term split.

Edition for 2026-27: News (DT Next, Sep 2026) says the new SEP-based syllabus applies only to classes 1-3 in 2026-27, so Std 10 should continue with the 2019 book (revised 2020/2021, annual reprints). A file labelled '2025 Edition' circulates but could not be opened, so later minor revisions after 2021 cannot be ruled out. Std 10 is not listed among the 2026-27 'new' books on third-party sites.

Reduced syllabus: TN reduced the SSLC syllabus in the Covid years (e.g. 2021-22 retained only parts of units: 1.1-1.4, 2.1-2.4/2.6-2.7, 3.1-3.6/3.8, 4.1-4.6, 5.1-5.5, 6.1/6.3, 7.1-7.4, 8.4-8.5 per a secondary copy). The full syllabus was restored for the 2023 public exams (secondary news). No reduction notice for 2025-26 or 2026-27 was found, and the dge.tn.gov.in notices could not be read. One secondary page (getmyuni) still shows a 'deleted syllabus 2026' table with no official citation, so I treated it as stale.
Exam pattern (secondary, careers360): SSLC Mathematics 100 marks, 2.5 hours plus 15 minutes reading time, pass mark 35. The official blueprint/question-pattern document was not verified.

Section 3.7 'Graph of Variations' appears in the 2021 revised contents but not in the 2019 first-edition chapter file. In that file 3.7 was Quadratic Graphs and 3.8 Matrices, and the matrix section looked shorter. The section list follows the revised contents.

Section lists contain only the numbered top-level sections from the official contents page. Sub-topics (nature of roots, relation between roots and coefficients, alternate segment theorem, tangent constructions, Ceva/Menelaus, standard deviation methods, tree diagrams) were confirmed from chapter files or secondary indexes and appear in the outcomes.
Several TN Grade 10 topics are Grade 11/12 in the competency list (sets/relations/functions, GP, matrices, straight lines, dispersion, event algebra). They are mapped by skill.

Proposed competencies cover topics with no existing equivalent: function composition, modular arithmetic, special series sums, three-variable linear systems, polynomial GCD/LCM (shared with Grade 9), rational expressions, polynomial square root, roots-coefficients relations, quadratic graphs, Pythagoras theorem, Ceva/Menelaus, coordinate polygon area, frustum. MATH.geometry.pythagoras may duplicate a proposal from another board/grade file, so check before merging.

Constructions of triangles from base, vertical angle and median/altitude/bisector are mapped partially to MATH.geometry.construction-triangles and MATH.geometry.circle-theorems rather than proposing a new competency.

sections.title: Identifying the Graphs of Linear, Quadratic, Cubic and Reciprocal Functions

outcomes.statement: Form ordered pairs and Cartesian products of two or three sets and find the number of elements in a product.

competencies.why: n(A × B × C) is counted in apcartn (v = 1), and listing the ordered pairs or triples and equal ordered pairs are the new apcartl and apcarteq; all are in the cartesian-product competency, which the outcome is not mapped to.

outcomes.statement: Identify relations as subsets of a Cartesian product and state their domain, co-domain and range.
Decide whether a relation is a function using arrow diagrams, ordered pairs, tables, rules and the vertical line test, and represent functions in these forms.
Classify functions as one-one, many-one, onto, into or bijective, and recognise constant, identity and real-valued functions.

competencies.why: Classifying functions as one-one, onto and bijective on ℕ, ℤ and ℝ is aqonto (function-types); many-one/into and constant/identity functions are now named in aofname (MATH.algebra.functions).

outcomes.statement: Form and evaluate compositions of functions and check whether composition is commutative or associative for given functions.

proposed.name: Compose functions
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.functions covers domain/range and MATH.algebra.inverse-functions covers inverses; forming f∘g, evaluating it and testing non-commutativity/associativity is a separate assessable skill not listed.

outcomes.statement: Recognise and sketch graphs of linear, modulus, quadratic, cubic, reciprocal and constant functions.

sections.title: Sum to n terms of a Geometric Progression

outcomes.statement: Apply Euclid's division lemma and algorithm to find the HCF of integers and to prove statements about integer forms.
Use the fundamental theorem of arithmetic to factorise numbers, find HCF and LCM, and reason about divisibility and terminating decimals.
Use congruence modulo n to find remainders, solve simple congruences and model cyclic situations such as clock times and weekdays.

proposed.name: Use congruence modulo n
proposed.why: No existing competency covers congruence modulo n, modular addition/multiplication or solving simple congruences (e.g. clock/day-of-week problems).

outcomes.statement: Find terms of sequences from general or recursive rules, and find nth terms, number of terms and conditions for arithmetic progressions.
Find the sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic series and solve related word problems.
Find nth terms of geometric progressions, sums of finite and infinite geometric series, and solve related problems.
Evaluate sums of the first n natural numbers, odd numbers, squares and cubes using standard formulas.

proposed.name: Sum special series of natural numbers
proposed.why: Using closed forms for sums of first n natural numbers, odd numbers, squares and cubes is not covered by the AP or GP competencies.

sections.title: Simultaneous Linear Equations in Three Variables

outcomes.statement: Solve a system of three linear equations in three variables by elimination and recognise systems with no or infinitely many solutions.

proposed.name: Solve linear systems in three variables
proposed.why: MATH.algebra.linear-systems is explicitly about pairs of equations; elimination for three unknowns (and recognising no/infinitely many solutions) is a genuine extension; MATH.algebra.matrix-systems is the Grade-12 matrix method, not elimination.

outcomes.statement: Find the GCD and LCM of polynomials and use the relation that their product equals the product of the two polynomials.

proposed.name: Find GCD and LCM of polynomials
proposed.why: No existing competency covers finding common divisors/multiples of polynomials; factorisation and factors-multiples are prerequisites, not the skill itself.

outcomes.statement: Reduce rational expressions to lowest terms, state excluded values, and multiply, divide, add and subtract rational expressions.

proposed.name: Simplify and operate on rational expressions
proposed.why: No existing competency covers reducing algebraic fractions, excluded values, and their four operations.

outcomes.statement: Find the square root of a perfect-square polynomial by factorisation and by the long-division method.

proposed.name: Find square roots of polynomials
proposed.why: Extracting the square root of a perfect-square polynomial (by factorisation or the long-division method) is not covered by any existing competency.

outcomes.statement: Solve quadratic equations by factorisation, completing the square and the formula, and apply them to word problems.

Analyse the roots of a quadratic without fully solving it: use the discriminant to determine their nature and find parameter values, and use the sum and product of roots to form equations and evaluate symmetric expressions.

proposed.name: Relate roots and coefficients of quadratics
proposed.why: Sum/product of roots, forming a quadratic from given roots and evaluating symmetric functions of roots are not in MATH.algebra.quadratics (solving) or MATH.algebra.quadratic-discriminant (nature of roots).

outcomes.statement: Draw graphs of direct and inverse variation, and plot quadratic graphs to solve quadratic equations, including by intersection with a straight line.

proposed.name: Solve quadratics graphically
proposed.why: Plotting y = ax^2+bx+c from a table and reading solutions (including via intersection with a line) is a graphical skill distinct from algebraic solving; no existing competency covers parabola plotting.

outcomes.statement: Identify the order and types of matrices, and add, subtract, scalar-multiply, multiply and transpose matrices, verifying their properties.

competencies.why: Transposes (of products, and symmetric/skew-symmetric parts) are assessed in the transpose-symmetry competency; the order and type of a matrix and constructing Aᵀ are now in apmtype and apmcon (MATH.algebra.matrices).

sections.title: Thales Theorem and Angle Bisector Theorem

outcomes.statement: Use AA, SAS and SSS similarity criteria and results on ratios of altitudes, perimeters and areas of similar triangles to solve problems.
Construct a triangle similar to a given triangle for a given scale factor less than or greater than 1.
Prove and apply the basic proportionality (Thales) theorem, the angle bisector theorem, and their converses.
Construct a triangle given its base, vertical angle and either the median, the altitude, or the point where the vertical-angle bisector meets the base.
Prove the Pythagoras theorem and its converse and apply them, including Pythagorean triples.

proposed.name: Apply the Pythagoras theorem and its converse
proposed.why: The competency list has no entry for the Pythagoras theorem (statement, converse, triples, applications); triangle-properties (Grade 6) and similarity do not name it. Check whether another board file already proposed the same id.

outcomes.statement: Apply tangent properties (radius–tangent perpendicularity, equal tangents from an external point, alternate segment theorem, common tangents) to find lengths and angles.
Construct a tangent at a point on a circle and a pair of tangents from an external point, and measure their lengths.
Apply Ceva's theorem to test concurrency of cevians and Menelaus' theorem to test collinearity, and find unknown segment ratios.

proposed.name: Apply Ceva and Menelaus theorems
proposed.why: Concurrency (Ceva) and collinearity (Menelaus) ratio conditions are not covered by any existing geometry competency.

sections.title: General Form of a Straight Line

outcomes.statement: Find the area of a triangle and of a quadrilateral from the coordinates of their vertices, and use zero area to test collinearity.

proposed.name: Find polygon areas from coordinates
proposed.why: MATH.coordinate.distance covers distance and section formulas only; area of a triangle/quadrilateral from vertex coordinates and the area test for collinearity are not covered.

outcomes.statement: Find the slope of a line from its inclination or from two points, and use slopes to test parallelism, perpendicularity and collinearity.
Write the equation of a straight line in slope-intercept, point-slope, two-point and intercept forms, including lines parallel to the axes.
Convert between general form ax+by+c=0 and other forms, read slope and intercepts, and find equations of lines parallel or perpendicular to a given line.
Use coordinate methods to solve geometric problems such as finding vertices, altitudes or the type of a quadrilateral.
Recall trigonometric ratios and their values for standard and complementary angles as a basis for identities.
Prove trigonometric identities using the Pythagorean identities and the reciprocal and quotient relations.
Use identities to simplify expressions and find values of other ratios from given conditions.
Solve height and distance problems involving angles of elevation, depression, or both, including two-observation problems.

sections.title: Volume and Surface Area of Combined Solids
Conversion of Solids from one Shape to another with no change in Volume

outcomes.statement: Calculate curved and total surface areas of solid and hollow cylinders.
Calculate surface areas and volumes of right circular cones, spheres, hemispheres and hollow hemispheres/spherical shells.
Calculate surface area and volume of a frustum of a cone.

proposed.name: Calculate frustum surface area and volume
proposed.why: Frustum formulas (curved/total surface area, volume) are not part of cones-spheres or combined-solids, which deal with whole solids.

outcomes.statement: Find surface areas and volumes of solids formed by combining cylinders, cones, spheres and hemispheres.
Solve problems where a solid is melted or recast into another shape using conservation of volume.
Find the range and coefficient of range of a data set and explain what dispersion measures.
Compute variance and standard deviation for raw, ungrouped and grouped data by direct, mean, assumed-mean and step-deviation methods.
Compute the coefficient of variation and use it to compare the consistency of two data sets.
List sample spaces of random experiments using tree diagrams and find probabilities of events.
Use the algebra of events (union, intersection, complement) and types of events (mutually exclusive, complementary, sure, impossible) to compute probabilities.
Apply the addition theorem of probability for two and three events to solve problems.
